back: A value that is much larger or much smaller than the rest of the data.

front: Which is affected more by an outlier: the mean or the median?
back: The mean. The median (and the IQR) hardly change.
The overall direction of the data, e.g. values rising over time or as another variable increases.
The natural differences between values. Another set of data would give slightly different results by chance.

front: What three parts should a good statistical statement have?
back: A claim, evidence (statistics with units) and context.
Data varies and groups overlap, so claims must allow for uncertainty.
When the way data is collected makes results lean one way, e.g. the people asked aren't representative.
A survey question that pushes people towards an answer, e.g. "Don't you agree…?"

front: Why is a bar graph axis that doesn't start at 0 misleading?
back: It cuts off the bottom of the bars, so small differences look much bigger than they are.

front: A picture is doubled in height and width. How much bigger does it look?
back: Four times the area, even though the amount only doubled.

front: Does a relationship in a scatter plot prove one thing causes the other?
back: No. It shows the variables are related, not that one causes the other.

front: Questions to ask about how data was collected
back: Who was asked, how many, how the question was worded, and who collected it (and why).
